transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It's real nice to meet you, too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I hope I'm not being a bother, but... I guess what brings me in is I just don't seem to have the push I used to have. You know, for things I normally like doing, like my choir, or my quilting... or even just visiting folks. 

I know people are expecting me, and I feel just awful letting them down, I really do. But most days, I just end up sitting at home with the TV on low. It's nothing too serious, I don't think, I just... can't seem to get going. Is that... does that make sense to you, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
About how long have you been feeling this way?

Oh, my... well, I suppose it's been a little while now. I really hate to admit it, because I know I should have just pulled myself together sooner. I didn't want to make a fuss or be a bother to anyone. 

But... I think it's been building up since I retired from the school office. That was, oh, a little over two years ago now. I just kept hoping I'd bounce back on my own, you know? I hope I didn't wait too long to come see you. Does two years sound like an awful long time to let something like this go, Doctor? I feel so silly for not fixing it myself.
Did these feelings begin after your retirement?

Yes, Doctor... oh, I'm sorry if I jumbled my words a moment ago, I get a little nervous and I hope I wasn't being confusing. But yes, that's exactly right. It's been building up ever since I retired from the school office... which was just a little over two years back. 

I really thought it was just a normal part of slowing down after stopping work, you know? I tried my best to keep a good attitude and not let it get to me. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
During these past two years, have you felt down or low most days?

Oh... well, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't feel sad or... or miserable, if that's what you mean. I really do try to count my blessings every day, and I know I have so much to be thankful for. I certainly don't want to sound ungrateful or like I'm complaining about my life. 

It's really just... well, the energy just isn't there like it used to be. But I'm not sitting around crying or feeling heartbroken or anything like that, oh goodness no. I hope I didn't make it sound like I was being a grump or feeling sorry for myself, Doctor. Am I explaining the difference alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you been diagnosed with any new medical condition around the time this loss of motivation started?

Oh, goodness, no. I haven't had any new sicknesses or anything like that. I always make sure to go to my regular checkups, I try to be very good about following my regular doctor's orders. So my physical health has been just fine, thank the Lord. 

I almost feel a little bad saying that, though... because if I'm perfectly healthy, I really don't have a good excuse for being so sluggish, do I? I just hope you don't think I'm just being lazy, Doctor. I really am trying my best to keep busy. Is it okay that there isn't a physical reason for it? I hope I'm not wasting your time.
After you adjusted to retirement, did this lack of motivation keep going?

Yes, Doctor. I know I mentioned it just a little bit ago, but it really has just been building up this whole time since I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now... and it just never really went away. 

I kept thinking that once I got my bearings and got used to being home, I'd bounce right back to my old self. But it just sort of kept going, exactly like you said. I feel a little silly admitting that I haven't quite shaken it off yet. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just not trying hard enough to adjust to my new life, because I really am trying to keep a good routine. Do a lot of folks take this long to get used to things, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
During this time, have you felt badly about yourself?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I mean, I certainly don't think poorly of myself. I know I have my flaws, just like anyone else, but I try to keep a positive attitude about who I am. I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around being hard on myself or feeling worthless, because that's not it at all. 

I just... well, I just feel a little guilty sometimes that I'm not doing more with my days, but that's just because I know I should be more productive. But I definitely don't hate myself or anything awful like that. I hope that makes sense, Doctor? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I'm feeling.
During these past two years, was there ever a period when you felt depressed or unable to enjoy things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed. I mean, I know I've been a bit slow to get moving, like we talked about, but I still try to find the good in things. I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around crying all day or anything like that. 

I still enjoy my little routines, you know? I like watching my shows and having my tea. I might not have the energy to do as much as I used to, but I'm not... I'm not miserable. I really do try to keep a smile on my face and not let things get me down. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill, Doctor.
Has this loss of motivation been causing problems in your daily life?

Well, oh, I wouldn't say it's causing real problems, exactly. I mean, I'm still getting by just fine on my own. But I suppose... well, I did decide to step back from leading the church choir recently. And I used to help out with the little projects down at the senior center, but... well, I just wasn't keeping up with the things I promised I would do. I felt just awful about it, so I thought it was best to let someone else take over, just so I wouldn't let anyone down. 

My friends from church have started checking on me a little more than they used to, which is very sweet of them, though I do hate to be a bother to anyone. It's perfectly okay to take a little break from volunteering when you're my age, isn't it, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by taking some time to rest.
Over the past two years, have you felt sad or down most days?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say I've been sad most days at all. I mean, sure, everyone gets a little blue every now and then, but I always try to look on the bright side. I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm just sitting in my chair moping all the time, because I'm really not. I try to count my blessings and keep a pleasant attitude. It's always better to focus on the good things, don't you think, Doctor? I just... I want to make sure I'm doing my part to stay as positive as I can.
After you retired, did this loss of motivation continue for more than six months?

Well, yes, I suppose it has been quite a while. It's... it's been building up since I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now. I didn't want to make a fuss about it, because I know adjusting to retirement takes time, and I didn't want anyone to think I was just being lazy. But yes, it's been going on since then. That's a normal part of getting older and stopping work, isn't it, Doctor? I just hope I haven't let it go on too long without saying something.
Do you feel that the stress of retiring has already passed?

Oh, well... I'm really not sure, to be perfectly honest. I haven't really thought about it quite like that. I wouldn't want you to think I've been sitting around feeling terribly stressed out or anything, because I do try to take things in stride. 

It's just... well, it's a big change, not having a place to be every morning after all those years. I suppose I don't really know if the adjustment part has completely passed or not. But I try my best not to let it get to me. It's better to just take each day as it comes and not complain, isn't it, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm handling everything the right way.
Do you feel your loss of motivation has been stronger than you would expect for adjusting to retirement?

Oh, I... I don't think so. I really wouldn't want to make it sound worse than it is. I mean, I imagine it's just the normal way people feel when they finally stop working after so many years. It's just a little slump, I suppose, not anything terribly unusual or... or extreme. 

I certainly try my best to push through it so I'm not just being a bother or acting helpless. That's just a normal part of adjusting to this stage of life, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill, Doctor.
Do you still feel retirement is an ongoing source of stress for you?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I really wouldn't call it a stress anymore. I mean... it's been a couple of years now, so I ought to be used to it, shouldn't I? 

I certainly don't want to sit here and sound ungrateful for having the time to rest. I think the hard part of the change is... well, it's behind me now. I mostly just keep to myself and try not to be a bother to anyone. So I really wouldn't say it's a stress at all. That means I'm doing okay with that part, right, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm handling it the way I'm supposed to.
